summary: Register Saleor as a self-hosted, GraphQL-only storefront provider (products/inventory/prices/orders/returns) authenticated with a single long-lived App bearer token, reusing the existing host-injected registry boundary.

impacts.evidence: Saleor accounts are tenant-scoped Connector SDK accounts identical in shape to woocommerce/medusa/shopware/magento; the store host, channel slug and warehouse slug are admin-supplied per-account non-secret runtime config, the same pattern every self-hosted storefront connector already uses.
The App access token stays behind the existing SecretAccessor/UseSecret boundary; product/order projections retain only bounded remote ids, numbers, statuses and amounts.

Saleor reuses the existing generic product/price sync machinery verbatim; no new public HTTP/OpenAPI operation is added. Saleor's own API is GraphQL-only, but this is entirely internal to the connector's own transport shape and does not change any host-facing contract.
No EventBus schema is added or changed.

Connector SDK root Connector/Runtime remain frozen; Saleor implements only existing capability-specific ports, no port is added or changed. Like Magento's Integration token, Saleor's App token is a single long-lived bearer credential with no runtime OAuth exchange or refresh, so no OAuth runtime (ADR-0104/ADR-0108) interaction was needed or made.
No schema change; Saleor uses the same generic non-secret runtime-config store every runtime_config_template connector already uses.

Fixed admin-supplied host, opaque bearer token behind SecretAccessor, bounded inputs and normalized errors preserve the provider boundary. Product create and webhook receipt return a normalized unsupported error with no faked success: webhook receipt was investigated in depth (Saleor's real JWS/RS256 signing mechanism was identified and traced to Saleor's own core source) and found to structurally exceed this SDK's 256-byte webhook signature envelope, not merely assumed unsupported by precedent.
products.write/prices.write/inventory.write/orders.status.write remain gated by the same capability checks every storefront connector already uses.
Writes flow through the existing fetch-compare-write-reconcile receipt path; no new evidence shape is introduced.

Writes follow the existing fetch-compare-write-reconcile pattern (see docs/connectors/saleor/reconciliation.md), extended to cover Saleor's multi-mutation product write (SKU/name/publication are three separate mutations, not one PUT); ambiguous transport failures reconcile against a re-fetch rather than retrying blindly.

Outbound authority is the admin-configured store host only, DNS-pinned through the existing SSRF-safe transport; inbound webhook receipt is explicitly unsupported in this task (see capability-audit.md), not silently unverified.

Non-2xx responses and malformed bodies are normalized to bounded errors; Saleor's GraphQL-specific error envelope (top-level errors[].extensions.exception.code, distinct from HTTP status) is normalized to the same sdk.RemoteError taxonomy every other connector uses.
Saleor can be disabled by removing its connector accounts; no schema rollback is needed.

Provider tests, go build/vet/test and the Task-064 conformance candidate pass 12 of 13 checks -- sandbox_isolation could not be exercised because this execution environment cannot create unprivileged Linux user namespaces, an environment constraint shared by every connector's Task-029 probe. docs/connectors/saleor/conformance-report.json records this genuine result rather than a fabricated pass.
